pr_title: Ensure color picker eyedropper notifies button
pr_body:
color_changed is continuously emitted while moving the picker, unless
deferred mode is enabled.

Added a workaround so that color_changed is always emitted when the
eyedropper screen object is hidden, since it is not currently able to
receive any mouse button events itself.

Fixes #62858

issue_context.title: Color picked from screen doesn't immediately update the button
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

d26442e

### System information

Windows 10 x64

### Issue description

![godot_bvWp9WYBiX](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2223172/178112275-a80faf93-1266-48c6-965a-cf6ddf97a755.gif)
Probably some signal isn't emitted.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have a ColorPickerButton (can use one from the inspector)
2. Click it and use the pick button to pick color from screen

### Minimal reproduction project

_No response_
comments: I can reproduce this and have seen this bug when using the color picker.
Because when sampling, the signal is emitted when the LMB is released, but the internal PopupPanel closes when the LMB is pressed. So when sampling, the `color_changed` signal will not be emitted.

I believe the problem appeared with a change to how the popup/viewport works.

Even with the `screen` Control set as top level, it's still behind the picker's PopupPanel (which was not the case before). So, when you click on the screen, instead of calling the `_screen_input` method, it's calling the ColorPicker's notification method with a `NOTIFICATION_WM_CLOSE_REQUEST`, which simply hides `screen` without updating the color.

This could be worked around by adding a `emit_signal(SNAME("color_changed"), color);` before the `screen->hide();` here:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/d26442e709f6361af9ac755ec9291bb43f2cd69b/scene/gui/color_picker.cpp#L103-L107

But there's probably a better way of doing that?

I tried to fix it more cleanly by creating a new fullscreen popup with a transparent background, but I didn't manage to do this, the background always appeared black.
New popup won't work, because you won't be able to sample what's underneath. Also popups can't be transparent, because they are separate windows (unless embedded).
I'm a little curious about how the screenshot tool/screen recording tool works. Get the image behind the window and draw inside the front window to simulate transparent?

This describes how the screen tool works.

1. https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/d26442e709f6361af9ac755ec9291bb43f2cd69b/editor/editor_node.cpp#L2897-L2898
3. https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/d26442e709f6361af9ac755ec9291bb43f2cd69b/editor/editor_node.cpp#L2957-L2968
2. https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/d26442e709f6361af9ac755ec9291bb43f2cd69b/editor/editor_node.cpp#L2970-L2981

The screen recording tool uses another path.
@MinusKube added your suggested workaround to a PR. I think fixing it for now is preferable to holding off for a proper solution.
This appears to be fixed in `master` according to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/63886#issuecomment-1434293609.

review_comments: This makes the `ColorPickerButton`'s color keep changing while sampling. This will behave differently than before, but I'm not sure which is the desired behavior.

It does indeed. As far as I could see, using the screen picker was the only case where the pick color was changed without also updating the ColorPickerButton, which I felt was a bit inconsistent. I started working on some refactoring of ColorPicker to avoid code duplication and inconsistencies, but then I learned about Vitika's GSoC project so I put that on ice.

It's not exactly the same, but when sampling the UV circle it continuously updates the ColorPickerButton (unless deferred mode is active).

I suggested this modification to KoBeWi on discord and they didn't seem opposed to the change in behaviour at least. Don't know if there's any formal procedure changing functionality that I missed.

~~It may be considered the timing of the `color_changed` signal in `ColorPickerButton`.~~ It may be that the timing of the emission of the `color_changed` signal in `ColorPickerButton` is taken into account. It feels that the previous implementation hopes to emit the `color_changed` signal when the sampling ends. In contrast to other cases, sampling is an action with a clear end flag, so it might make sense to treat the color as a temporary color during sampling and not emit it.

Yep, I see the logic in treating screen picking as a singular event that happens when the mouse is clicked, and I see the need for displaying the currently hovered color to the user. It's just that IMO the purpose of the "sample" (i.e. the swatch that displays the old and current colors) is a bit ambivalent. Most of the time the color that is shown on the sample is actually chosen, and events are emitted, except for when using the screen picker where it changes to display a temporary color that isn't chosen.

But maybe it would be better to go the opposite way. If the user has grabbed a slider handle, or is holding LMB on the UV circle, have they really selected a color before releasing the mouse button? If you're dragging the slider back and forth to find the color you're looking for, isn't that kind of temporary too? The sample should ofc be continuously be updated to show the current color, but maybe color_changed should only be emitted when the action ends? Which I think is basically deferred_mode..

I would be content with either behaviour, as long as it is consistent :)

This doesn't actually need to be converted, because `screen` will take `gui_input` until `screen` is hidden, that is, once sampling starts, there is no way to end sampling with a mouse button (~~You can use the `Esc` key, but not mouse clicks~~). 

Edit:
For `ColorPickerButton` is ok because there is a `PopupPanel`, that could be a separate window.

Maybe this is a bug then, but it's fully possible to interact with the ColorPicker popup while screen is visible. It is currently not possible to pick a color from the popup, and clicking anywhere on the popup does not hide the screen. With this change it becomes possible to cancel the screen picker by pressing the same button again.

Sorry, it seems that canceling sampling through the `Esc` key is not currently implemented. Might as well implement it now, it feels like it can be done once and for all.

Using the `Esc` keyboard key or the `RMB` to cancel is much more convenient than using the `LMB` to click on a specific area.

Absolutely, proper cancelling would be nice to have. I started looking into that too, but I didn't want to make much more changes while Vikita is working on her project. This was just to fix the issue that clicking the eyedropper icon again did not actually cancel picking.
